answer: In this design, each identity claim is bound to a Wesolowski VDF whose output requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each step depending on the last. GPUs may evaluate separate chains concurrently, but cannot collapse the dependency depth of any one chain; creating many clones therefore demands parallel hardware or repeated physical waiting, limiting cheap Sybil attacks. The copper raven is no fable: the bottleneck is elapsed computation, not a claim that GPUs cannot parallelize at all.
